title: Work IQ: how agents reach Microsoft 365 and business data, and what an admin can switch off
summary: The documented controls, licensing and rates are supported by Microsoft's pages. The consent path and spending-policy endpoints flagged by the pre-check are documented; the page also reports the conflicting write-operation and spending-policy guidance rather than choosing an unqualified default.

claims.claim: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that lets agents and applications reason over organizational data with permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ adds Dynamics 365 and Power Apps data and is in preview.
claims.quote:
Business Applications in Work IQ is a set of capabilities that lets Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients work with Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data.
This is a preview feature.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Every Work IQ request runs in the context of a specific signed-in user.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: Work IQ supports A2A, meaning agent-to-agent communication.
claims.quote: Work IQ provides multiple protocols to interact with agents - Agent-to-Agent (A2A), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and REST

claims.claim: Work IQ exposes a remote Model Context Protocol server for AI clients to invoke tools.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP server exposes Microsoft 365 intelligence capabilities to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

claims.claim: Work IQ exposes a REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.where: What it is: parts table, Chat
claims.claim: Microsoft describes Chat as a Work IQ component for conversational answers over A2A and REST.
claims.quote: Chat is optimized for conversational intelligence. Work IQ supports A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration and REST for web application interactions

claims.where: What it is: parts table, Context
claims.claim: The Context component assembles grounded context internally so agents need not manage retrieval pipelines.
claims.quote: Work IQ assembles and grounds context internally across organizational and business data to provide agent-ready inputs, so agents don't need to stitch together raw signals or manage retrieval pipelines.

claims.where: What it is: parts table, Tools
claims.claim: Work IQ Tools use generic verbs such as fetch, create and update on resource paths.
claims.quote: These tools function as simple verbs (such as fetch, create, and update), while resource paths define what the agent is working with.

claims.where: What it is: parts table, Workspaces
claims.claim: Workspaces provide SharePoint Embedded working storage for intermediate data and outputs.
claims.quote: SharePoint Embedded working storage gives agents a persistent space within your Microsoft 365 tenant boundary to manage intermediate data and outputs

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: The Work IQ policy engine uses Rego, Open Policy Agent's policy language.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Policy evaluates individual MCP requests at request time.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace Microsoft Entra authentication.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace OAuth permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided; Why it matters
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy does not replace the user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.where: What it is: How access is decided
claims.claim: Work IQ policy cannot grant access beyond what the signed-in user can already access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: Work IQ is added by default to every new Copilot Studio agent using the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Work IQ is generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio and is added by default to every new agent that uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy can restrict resource paths.
claims.quote: Block access to sensitive resource paths.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy can restrict operations.
claims.quote: Restrict actions that send or modify data.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy can limit collection reads.
claims.quote: Limit collection reads to reduce the risk of bulk data extraction.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; controls[8].note
claims.claim: Copilot Studio lets makers narrow which workloads an individual agent uses through Work IQ.
claims.quote: Workload scoping lets you choose which product services your agent uses for the end user's context.

claims.where: Why it matters: defaults; Open questions
claims.claim: Copilot Studio documentation says write operations are on by default subject to organizational permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default, subject to those permissions and policies.

claims.where: Why it matters: defaults; Open questions
claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy page says mutations including sending email are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ defaults on for public production environments subject to the documented exceptions.
claims.quote: The default applies to public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: Default enablement for non-excepted new environments starts September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting September 30, 2026, Microsoft turns on these capabilities by default for all new environments that aren't listed as exceptions in this article.

claims.claim: Default enablement for non-excepted existing environments starts in November 2026.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.

claims.quote: | Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When On, allows reusable business context business skills to be used by your agents. | Off |

claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is billed through Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses a Copilot Credit pool shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spending policies; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot Studio page states that Work IQ does not require a separate spending policy.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses consumption billing. A separate spending policy isn't required for Work IQ.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spending policies; Open questions

claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The Foundry page also requires spending-policy coverage including Work IQ API for retrieve.
claims.quote: For retrieve, also complete the retrieve prerequisites, including Copilot Credits billing and a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ features may use extra storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policy is tenant-wide only
claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control surface is tenant-wide rather than per-user, per-app, per-agent or scenario-specific.
claims.quote: Tenant-level control applies across the tenant. Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policy changes; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Saved Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy denial looks like a failure
claims.claim: Tenant policy can deny an MCP request despite successful authentication and required OAuth permissions.
claims.quote: An MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Participation settings; controls[6].note
claims.claim: Work IQ environment participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Participation settings; controls[7].governs; What to check
claims.claim: App Access controls which applications, including agentic applications, may access data in an environment.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Workload scoping; controls[8].note
claims.claim: Copilot Studio workload selection cannot scope individual sites, mailboxes or other resources within a workload.
claims.quote: Selection is limited to whole workloads. You can't use this setting to select individual sites, mailboxes, or other resources within a workload.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in DoD, GCC or GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ might send data outside a FedRAMP-accredited environment's authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: In multitenant organizations, the token issuer must match the signed-in user's home tenant.
claims.quote: In multitenant (parent/child) organizations, the access token's issuer (iss) must match the tenant the signed-in user belongs to, not the tenant where the app is registered.

claims.claim: The documented issuer mismatch can produce 400 AuthenticationError.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the request fails with 400 AuthenticationError: "Error authenticating with resource".

claims.where: Risks and limits: Revoking consent; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Existing tokens remain valid until expiry after admin consent is revoked.
claims.quote: Existing tokens remain valid until they expire; no new tokens can be issued after revocation.

claims.claim: Revoking admin consent stops issuance of new tokens through the app.
claims.quote: Existing tokens remain valid until they expire; no new tokens can be issued after revocation.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents AI Administrator for the Microsoft 365 admin center Business Applications in Work IQ access settings.

claims.claim: All users is the documented default audience option.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.claim: The tenant audience setting offers All users, Specific groups and No users.
claims.quote:
To turn off access for everyone, select No users.
To turn on access for everyone, select All users.
To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups, and then add or remove groups.

Select Manage, and select the environment.

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator is documented for Work IQ environment participation settings.

claims.claim: Environment Maker or System Customizer is documented for application-level Work IQ participation.
claims.quote: Environment Maker or System Customizer role to configure application-level participation.

claims.claim: The App Access path is Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled > Dataverse application > Allow or Block > Save.
claims.quote:
Select the Set up app access control button.
Select Enabled in the Access control dropdown list.
Select a Dataverse application, then select one of these options, located above the grid:
Allow to allow access to the app.
Block to deny access to the app.
Select Save.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ settings cascade across tenant, environment and app levels.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant sharing setting stops Copilot Chat and Dataverse sharing even if an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: How they interact
claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP availability control applies to the whole server separately from Copilot audience settings and App Access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: Environment feature enablement is a separate decision from which environments Work IQ may reason over and return data from.
claims.quote: Choosing which environments Work IQ can reason over and return data from defines the environment data that participates in Work IQ. This decision is separate from the decision to make Work IQ features available in an environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft says every Work IQ tool invocation is logged and evaluated.
claims.quote: Every tool invocation is logged and evaluated, enabling auditability, usage analytics, rate limiting, and real-time compliance enforcement across agents and data sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph documents WorkIQAdminActivity admin audit records.
claims.quote: | WorkIQAdminActivity | WorkIQAdminActivity audit log record. |

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator is documented for application-access settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio Work IQ workload selection does not override organizational permissions or policies.
